newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet zooms higher, diesel mixed.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet zooms higher, diesel mixed.

text.p: Singapore physical jet fuel prices zoomed higher on talk regional supplies have been nearly exhausted until end-February, while gas oil prices were mixed as a trader tried to offer lower, traders said on Wednesday.
Indonesia provided the support for the jet fuel market, but some traders said earlier estimates it had bought 2.5 million barrels appeared too high.
They estimated that Indonesia has bought around 1.5 million barrels and might seek one or two more cargoes.
Indonesia's normal monthly imports were less than one million barrels, traders said.

A European major last week sold 120,000 barrels of jet fuel to Indonesia at 53 cents a barrel above Singapore spot quotes free-on-board (fob) basis for end-February lifting. Sellers said the 53-cent premium was a good price to sell.
Traders said that despite the ebbing winter demand in North Asia, there was still a trickling of demand from that region.

There was active buying interest in the Singapore jet fuel market on Wednesday with three bids seen, starting at $29.20 but a trade finally took place between a Singapore trader and a Swiss trader at a higher price of $30.40. The 100,000-barrel parcel is for Feb 13-17 lifting fob.
Gas oil was also actively discussed at wide ranges with a major offering as high as $26.45 a barrel and a local trader offering as low as $24.90 for second-half February lifting fob.
A 150,000-barrel lot of gas oil was sold by the same Singapore trader to a European major at $25.20, below Tuesday's trade of $25.40.

Traders said the number of gas oil sellers underlined the soft market with activity in China at a standstill while stocks are high in Hong Kong. Indonesia's jet fuel demand was not matched by its demand for gas oil.
Gas oil oil swaps slipped 25 cents in late trading from earlier levels to $25.55/$25.75 for February.
